c_isolation.method: every query is scoped with an explicit --project; no --all anywhere; another project's output is never stored
c_isolation.neutral_cwd_evidence: for a neutral cwd the CLI reports which project it derived, so the record shows the call was attributed to the neutral directory and not to isswf
c_isolation.foreign_project_stdout_policy: parsed for counts and title presence only, raw output discarded

repo_cwd_without_project_observation.note: Informational, not an assertion. The repository directory is named isSWF, so an unprojected call made from inside it is expected to resolve to the isswf project and to return our own memories. The required isolation property is the neutral-cwd result above.

cwd_detection_probe_on_disposable_store.purpose: measure how Engram derives the project when --project is absent, without touching the real store

basename_probe.save_command: /home/iseoane/.local/bin/engram save 'basename probe' 'marker for cwd derivation' --type note --scope project

disposable_store_control.purpose: same isolation question on a disposable store where every selector exists and holds memories, so a zero result cannot come from a missing project
disposable_store_control.real_store_difference: on the real store the neutral cwd is a random directory whose derived project does not exist, so the CLI answers No memories found with exit 0; here the derived project exists and holds the decoy, which makes the marker's absence a real filter result

proven: Two memories with the given title, body, project and scope are stored in the real store and retrieved back by search and context.
A query scoped to another project, and a query from a neutral cwd without --project, return none of the isSWF memories.
isSWF's suite, CLI walkthrough and SQLite content are identical with Engram unusable and with Engram available.
not_proven: That isSWF consumes Engram at runtime: isswf/ and tests/ contain no reference to Engram, so the closed-failure result shows absent coupling, not a graceful degradation path inside isSWF.
Anything about MCP transport, cloud sync, memory conflict resolution, or the shared store's behaviour under a hostile process of the same user.
That the memories were not modified or deleted later, or that other sessions do not read the shared store's other projects.
Any claim about the store's other projects beyond the single reference name and its observation count.
notes: The suite and the walkthrough use absolute sys.executable, so the broken PATH isolates Engram only.
The store is shared with a running engram serve process whose cwd is agent-depot; every isSWF query passes an explicit --project.
No memory was deleted, no --hard and no --all was used, and sync.log and other projects' configuration were not touched.
The search and context views truncate a long body on screen; the stored text is verified exactly through the project's own export, not the display.
The recorded commit is HEAD at execution time, not necessarily the commit named in the briefing.
